explanation: Item corresponds to idea: item is a tangible entity that can be touched, while idea is an abstract and intangible thought. Both can be used and communicated.
Hold corresponds to understand: holding an item is to grasp it in your hand, while understanding an idea is to grasp it in your mind. Both indicate the mastery and understanding of an object.
Weigh corresponds to analyze: weighing measures the weight of an object, while analyzing evaluates the value and meaning of an idea. Both indicate the process of evaluating an object.
Heavy corresponds to important: a heavy object has a large mass in material terms, while an important idea has a great value in terms of thought. Both indicate a degree of importance and value.
Light corresponds to trivial: a light object has a small mass in material terms, while a trivial idea has a small value in terms of thought. Both indicate a degree of slightness and unimportance.

background.source: Objects are all around us; they are things we can touch, see, and sometimes even hear. An object can be anything, ranging from something as small as a pen to something as large as a car. Objects can hold other objects and can weigh both heavy and light. Every object has its unique characteristics and features, making it distinguishable from others. Whether we use objects in our daily lives or simply admire them from afar, they play an essential role in shaping our world.
background.target: An idea is a fundamental aspect of human cognition that encompasses the mental representation of objects or concepts. It is generated through thought and reflection, and can arise spontaneously without deliberate intent. While some ideas may seem trivial, many possess profound importance and have the potential to drive innovation and transformation. The ability to understand and analyze ideas is critical to comprehending the world around us and making meaningful contributions to society. Hence, exploring and nurturing new and original ideas is essential for personal and societal growth.
